description.description: One line: what the app does.

auth_methods.description: Every auth method a third-party developer can use for the public API.

auth_detail.description: Short detail, e.g. 'OAuth2 auth-code for public apps; private app token for single account'.

access.description: Most restrictive gate a developer hits to get WORKING credentials for a toolkit that end users can connect. self_serve_free = anyone can sign up and get keys free (free tier or free developer account/sandbox); self_serve_trial = anyone can sign up but only via a time-limited trial; paid_plan = public signup exists but API access needs a paid tier; admin_approval = developer can build, but the vendor must review/verify the app (or grant a developer token) before other users can connect it; customer_account = no public signup or developer sandbox: credentials only exist inside an existing (usually sales-led) customer account; partner_gated = partnership program, application, or contact-sales required for API access; no_public_api = no documented public API.

api_breadth.description: broad = most product objects covered (50+ endpoints); moderate = core objects; narrow = a handful of endpoints; none.

mcp_exists.description: Any MCP server exists (official or credible community).

mcp_official.description: An MCP server published by the vendor itself exists.

mcp_url.description: URL of the best MCP server found, or empty string.

verdict.description: build_now = a developer could ship an agent toolkit today with self-serve creds; build_with_caveat = buildable but limited (narrow API, paid plan, app review for public use); needs_outreach = partnership/sales/approval needed first; not_buildable = no usable API. Rule: customer_account or partner_gated with no free developer sandbox => needs_outreach.

blocker.description: Main blocker if not build_now, else empty string.

quote.description: Exact sentence copied verbatim from that URL (max ~200 chars). Must appear on the page.
